intended_object: The cover induced on an open subset V by a finite open cover 𝒱 = (V_α) of the whole space X, namely (V ∩ V_α)_α, which is a finite open cover of V. This is the restricted cover used in Leray's theorem (Forster §12–14), as the docstring and module doc say.
explanation:
`FinCover Ω` is the library's structure for a family of opens `U : Fin n → Opens X` that lie inside Ω and cover Ω. `FinCover.induced 𝒱 V` keeps the same index set `Fin 𝒱.n` and has members `V ⊓ 𝒱.U α`. Each member lies in V. Every x ∈ V is in some `𝒱.U α`, because 𝒱 covers ⊤. So the result is exactly the standard induced (restricted) cover (V ∩ V_α)_α of V.

Keeping the index set unchanged, including members that may be empty, is the usual convention. It is what you need so that cochains on 𝒱 restrict componentwise, as `indCocycle` does.

The section variables `ChartedSpace ℂ X` and `IsManifold` are not used by the body. Defs drop unused section variables, and the later simp lemmas mention `𝒱.induced V` after omitting those instances, which confirms they are not arguments. So the construction is purely topological, which is its natural generality.

Taking the cover of ⊤ instead of a cover of an arbitrary Ω containing V is the standard textbook setting: a cover of X restricted to an open subset. It is not a real loss of generality. Mathlib has no finite-cover structure of this kind and no induced-cover counterpart.
